economy.summary: His campaign platform says he will work to reduce the cost of groceries and everyday essentials to keep money in people's pockets, and to boost job training programs to provide opportunities for everyone in the region.
economy.short: Proposes reducing grocery and essentials costs; boosting job training programs.

education.summary: In a March 2025 interview during the special election campaign, he said his time on the McKeesport school board showed him how crucial it is that schools receive state funding and that the funding must be fair, and voiced concern that districts like McKeesport are losing millions of dollars a year to support charter schools.
education.short: Supports fair state school funding; concerned about charter school costs.

healthcare.summary: In a March 2025 interview he emphasized the need for more state support for EMS services that are struggling in the district; he has not detailed positions on broader healthcare topics.
healthcare.short: Supports more state funding for struggling EMS services.

guns.summary: As state representative he sponsored House Bill 2190 to extend binding arbitration rights to transit, campus, and certain state law enforcement officers, saying it would help keep communities safe by keeping more officers on the job; this is a public-safety measure, and he has not detailed a position on firearms policy.
guns.short: Sponsored bill extending police arbitration rights; no stated firearms position.
